## Maintainer ruling recorded — A: gate the share-link probe on the standing policy, at both sites

Director seat, summon #11, session `session_01ShyhexkB2d1AeRZ85tgAAe`, 2026-09-03.

Provenance (who / verbatim / where): maintainer, live PM chat with the director seat, 2026-09-03, replying to decision batch #17 in which this card was item 1 with the recommendation A (fallback B). Verbatim reply: 「同意」 — adopts the recommendation.

**Ruled: A.** The route probe reads `publicSharing.enabled` before it answers from the row; when sharing is off for the object, every arm falls through to the generic `404 INVALID_OR_EXPIRED` that unknown, revoked, expired and ineligible tokens already give — links on a switched-off object become indistinguishable from unknown tokens, which is the property `share-link-service` already states in prose. The fix lands at **both** probe sites in the same PR: `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/share-link-routes.ts` and the twin in `packages/runtime/src/domains/share-links.ts`; landing at one site only moves the oracle. Option B (keep the 401 and document the accepted oracle) is the recorded fallback and is not taken; option C (gate only the two 401 arms) is rejected as proliferation. The maintainer accepts the product consequence named in the confidence gap: for a link on a switched-off object the viewer sees "link invalid" rather than a password prompt — the correct behaviour, since a correct password on such a link yields nothing.

Execution: `domain:services` lane, M. **`Clause-②: yes`** — a published HTTP path changes its refusal for two link shapes (401 → 404), so the dispatch runs at the contract-review tier and the PR carries `needs:contract-review` for in-seat review before it is readied. Pins: both sites, both shapes (`password_hash`, `audience: 'signed_in'`), asserting byte-equality with the unknown-token answer; plus the reverse check. The `repo:objectui` viewer is not changed by this card; if the viewer keys a password prompt on `401 NEEDS_PASSWORD`, the services seat notes it in the PR body for the objectui seat — no cross-repo work is owed by this ruling.

State transition, same stroke: `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`. Ledger: director seat post #12708, summon #11.

B is the recorded fallback and is not taken; C is rejected.

`needs:contract-review` is hung on this card now, per the ruling's `Clause-②: yes`; it goes on the PR as well when it opens.

### ⚠️ Declared up front: this card will reach a gate that is currently closed

The contract-review tier is **unavailable** — an isolated review dispatched at that tier at 07:20Z today terminated on the provider's own refusal (HTTP 429, entitlement exhausted). Two cards are already frozen on it (#14353 / PR #14866, and #14333 / PR #14712).

So this dispatch is made with the consequence stated rather than discovered: **the work will be built and pushed, and the PR will then sit as a draft until the review can run.** It is dispatched anyway because the maintainer instructed the seat to continue dispatching, and because a ruled card built now is ready the moment the tier returns — but ⛔ this PR will not be undrafted or armed on CI colour alone.

Unlock is either of: the entitlement resets, or the maintainer routes the review through the director seat / decision-batch path, as was done for #14176 (PR #14776).

> Clause-②: yes

## Why this is being re-posted

Not a new claim and not a changed judgement — a **respelling of the existing one** so the landing pre-check can read it.

The original claim comment (`issuecomment-5522768375`) declared `Clause-② yes` correctly, but in two spellings no checker can parse: it opened `**Claim:**`, which fails `CLAIM_COMMENT_MARKER` (`/^\s*>?\s*Claim(?:ed)?\s*:/mi`, `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs:1056`) because of the leading `**` — so it was not recognised as a claim comment **at all** — and its reading was inline prose, which fails the line-anchored `CLAUSE2_KEY_LINE` (`scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs:244`).

Measured, not assumed — `node scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 14905` exits **4**:

> ✗ C2 — card #14637 (delivering open PR #14905 (draft)) — NO READING on the declaration limb: the card's claim comment carries no `Clause-②:` line in the fixed spelling. … A missing reading is NOT a declared `no`: one of those is a decision and the other is an absent one.

That is the failure mode the gate exists to catch and it was live on this card: a declared `yes` that reads to the machine as *nothing*, on a security change. Found by the tier contract review on PR #14905, §3 patch 3.

The script also says ⛔ do not fill the line in **on the claiming seat's behalf**. This seat **is** the claiming seat for this card, so this is that seat making its own declaration legible, not another seat writing it for them. The judgement is unchanged: **`yes`** — a published HTTP path changes its refusal for two link shapes and the revoked arm, exactly as the maintainer's ruling of record set it (comment 5522728999, option A, verbatim 「同意」).

⛔ The gate is report-only by design and this seat does not clear `needs:contract-review` from a checker's exit code — the contract review's verdict is `PASS WITH REQUIRED PATCHES`, and the carriers stay hung on both this card and PR #14905 until those patches land and the delta is re-read.
